memory_update.text: Murata/MRAAY should remain the reference anchor for the AI-server high-end MLCC sub-node, but it is not the main underfollowed U.S. discovery candidate because it is a large non-U.S. primary-listed component leader.

Vishay/VSH is a plausible underfollowed U.S.-listed second-order candidate for AI-server board-level power delivery via power inductors, capacitors, and discrete power components; direct AI-server revenue evidence is still required.

Bel Fuse/BELFB is a plausible underfollowed U.S.-listed candidate for data-center power/connectivity/magnetics exposure, especially around 48V distribution, power shelves, redundant power supplies, and connector modules.

Vicor/VICR has cleaner direct AI accelerator power-delivery mapping than most small/mid-cap names, but its market cap and attention level are higher; keep it as a pure-play power-delivery context name rather than an obscure-passives name.

Need a follow-up pass on U.S.-traded ADR/OTC passive-component leaders such as TDK, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo/KEMET, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Panasonic Industry to determine whether any are investable through U.S. tickers and whether AI-server MLCC/polymer-capacitor exposure is more direct than VSH/BELFB.

For this node, the highest-quality evidence to survive Layer 2 should be explicit AI-server/datacenter revenue acceleration, high-end MLCC or power-component capacity constraints, customer qualification cycles, ASP/mix improvement, backlog, or capex tied to server power-density demand.

node: AI-server high-end passives and board-level power delivery
summary: Expanded the AI-server high-end passives and board-level power-delivery node with a two-lane list. Murata is included as the reference-quality MLCC anchor because cached evidence directly ties it to high-capacitance, low-ESR/low-ESL AI-server MLCCs. The underfollowed lane focuses on U.S.-listed or U.S.-traded companies one step away from GPUs: Vishay for power inductors/capacitors and discrete power components, Bel Fuse for data-center power supplies/connectors/magnetics, and Vicor for high-density AI accelerator power conversion. Claims are deliberately conservative: direct AI-server exposure is strongest for Murata and Vicor, plausible but still evidence-needed for Vishay and Bel Fuse.
